title: WebSockets vs SSE vs Long Polling vs gRPC
subtitle: Choosing bidirectional vs server-push vs binary RPC transport
overview: Every real-time feature forces a transport choice. Short polling wastes bandwidth; Long Polling ties up HTTP handlers; Server-Sent Events (SSE) push cleanly over standard HTTP/2; WebSockets unlock full-duplex chat/gaming; and gRPC gives typed Protobuf binary RPCs for internal microservices.
firstPrinciplesStory: You build a live auction ticker using 1-second HTTP polling. With 500,000 open tabs, you suddenly get hit by 500,000 HTTP requests every second—99% returning 'no new bid', burning TLS handshakes and JSON parsing CPU for nothing! Switching to persistent server-push cuts traffic 50x—but choosing full WebSockets where one-way SSE suffices adds sticky-session draining headaches behind L7 proxies.

adaptiveLenses.intuition: Short polling is calling the restaurant every 5 seconds asking 'is my food ready?'. Long polling is staying on hold until they answer, then immediately redialing. SSE is a one-way intercom where the kitchen calls out updates over your existing phone line. WebSocket is a two-way walkie-talkie. gRPC is a compressed pneumatic tube between internal factory stations.
adaptiveLenses.mechanics: Long polling holds an HTTP request open up to ~30s until an event arrives, then reconnects. SSE streams `text/event-stream` with automatic `Last-Event-ID` resume over HTTP/2 multiplexing. WebSocket upgrades HTTP/1.1 (`101 Switching Protocols`) to raw bidirectional TCP frames. gRPC uses HTTP/2 streams + compact binary Protobuf contracts.
adaptiveLenses.staffTradeoffs: Always prefer SSE over WebSockets for unidirectional feeds (LLM token streams, stock tickers, build logs) because SSE rides seamlessly on standard HTTP/2 L7 load balancers and auto-reconnects natively. Reserve WebSockets for high-frequency bidirectional frames (chat typing, multiplayer cursors) and gRPC for strongly-typed internal east-west RPCs.

ddiaAnchors.chapter: DDIA Ch. 4 · Encoding & Service Data Flow
ddiaAnchors.whyItMatters: Typed Protobuf schemas with field tags prevent breaking rolling microservice deploys and shrink wire payloads.

pragmaticTips.tip: Don't deploy stateful WebSocket connection registries unless the client genuinely sends frequent upstream messages over the same socket.
pragmaticTips.application: Use SSE + normal HTTP POST for LLM chat; reserve WebSockets for bi-directional apps like WhatsApp or Figma.

keyTakeaways: SSE provides native reconnect (`Last-Event-ID`) and HTTP/2 L7 compatibility for server-to-client push.
WebSockets reduce per-frame overhead for true full-duplex chat and multiplayer collaboration.
gRPC accelerates internal service-to-service calls via Protobuf binary framing and HTTP/2 multiplexing.

nodes.label: Web / Mobile Client
nodes.summary: Maintains persistent stream for live token/message push.
failureModes: Mobile NAT timeouts drop idle sockets unless heartbeats run every 25–30s

nodes.label: L7 Edge Gateway
nodes.summary: Multiplexes SSE streams cleanly over HTTP/2 or terminates upgraded WebSocket TCP sockets.
failureModes: HTTP/1.1 browsers cap 6 SSE connections per domain unless HTTP/2 is enabled

nodes.label: Realtime Stream Service
nodes.summary: Consumes backend events over typed gRPC streams and flushes frames to edge clients.
whenToUse: Streaming AI tokens, live telemetry, chat fan-out
failureModes: Slow client read buffers bloat pod memory unless bounded write deadlines drop stalled consumers

nodes.label: Pub/Sub Event Bus
nodes.summary: Broadcasts updates to gateway pods holding active client subscriptions.
failureModes: Missed events during brief disconnect unless client sends Last-Event-ID catchup

predictPrompt.prompt: Why is SSE generally preferred over WebSockets for streaming ChatGPT-style LLM token output?
predictPrompt.hint: Think about traffic direction per turn and how L7 HTTP/2 proxies handle connections.
predictPrompt.reveal: LLM generation is strictly server-to-client after the prompt POST. SSE works natively over standard HTTP/2 L7 load balancers, supports browser auto-reconnect with Last-Event-ID, and avoids WebSocket proxy timeout quirks.

chaosScenarios.title: Mobile Network Drop & Last-Event-ID Seamless Resume
chaosScenarios.triggerSummary: Client subway tunnel drops connection for 8 seconds while events #403–#405 fire on the server.
chaosScenarios.mitigationSummary: Browser EventSource auto-reconnects passing `Last-Event-ID: 402`; Stream Service replays missed #403–#405 from Redis/Kafka buffer before resuming live push.

steps.info: Reconnect sends Last-Event-ID: 402 -> server replays missed #403..405 cleanly
steps.payloadInspector: Last-Event-ID: 402 -> Replay events [403, 404, 405] -> Resume live stream
steps.inspectorNote: Pairing Last-Event-ID with a short-lived replay log makes transient disconnects invisible to users.

cons: Stateful TCP pinning complicates L7 draining & autoscaling
